title: Named and default exports
learningObjectives: Explain named and default exports and build modular, event-driven browser code.

understand.concept: A module can export multiple named bindings and at most one default export. Named imports use matching exported names, while a default import can choose a local name. Exported bindings are live bindings rather than copied snapshots.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing clear exports makes dependencies easier to understand. Named exports support explicit imports; default exports can represent a module's primary value when that convention is useful.
understand.analogy: Named exports are individually labelled tools; a default export is the module's main item.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; module loading and DOM event behaviour follow web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The default function and named bindings are imported using their respective syntaxes.

examples.explanation: The default function and named bindings are imported using their respective syntaxes.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console output demonstrates module or event behaviour; DOM examples require matching elements.

practise.guidedTask: Create a module with two named exports and one default export. Import each and explain the syntax difference.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using explicit module boundaries or DOM event handling. Test keyboard, pointer, dynamic content, and failure cases as appropriate.
hints: Keep module responsibilities and public exports clear.
Preserve native keyboard and form behaviour.

questions.prompt: How is a default export imported?
options: With an import binding that does not use braces
questions.answer: With an import binding that does not use braces
questions.explanation: A default export is imported without the named-import braces.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for modular event-driven code?
options: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
Stop all propagation for every event
Expose every internal module binding globally
questions.answer: Use clear contracts and preserve expected browser behaviour
questions.explanation: Explicit interfaces and predictable event handling reduce coupling and preserve usability.
